2C.12 The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom.
3L.15 Do not reprove a fool or a scoffer, lest he hate you, for reprove is more effective for a wise man, and he also will love you for it.

precepts.text: The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old; I was set up from everlasting. Wisdom and Christ are interchangeable here, because Christ is the ultimate wisdom.
precepts.point: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars. Seven pillars: complete wisdom.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
“Wisdom hath builded her house”. Who is this wisdom? Go back a chapter, where wisdom speaks: “The Lord possessed me in the beginning of his way, before his works of old. I was set up from everlasting, from the beginning, or ever the earth was.”

This is going into Christ and wisdom, one and the same, interchangeable. Christ is the ultimate wisdom, the complete wisdom, set up from everlasting before the earth was.

That is why chapter 9 says wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Seven represents completion, and Christ is complete wisdom. The house wisdom built stands on him, the one the Lord possessed in the beginning of his way.

precepts.text: There shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse: count the seven upon him. The spirit of the Lord, wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of the Lord: the seven pillars, complete spiritual perfection, which is what Christ operated in.
precepts.point: Wisdom hath builded her house, she hath hewn out her seven pillars. Seven pillars: complete wisdom.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Wisdom “hath hewn out her seven pillars”. Let's see who this wisdom pertains to and who had these seven pillars. Isaiah: “And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots”. That is talking about Christ.

Now count what rests upon him. “And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him”: that's one. “the spirit of wisdom”: two. “and understanding”: three. “the spirit of counsel”: four. “And might”: five. “the spirit of knowledge”: six. “and of the fear of the Lord”: seven.

Those are the seven pillars of wisdom that Christ had. Seven represents completion, so they represent complete spiritual perfection, and that is what Christ operated in. Wisdom's house on seven pillars is Christ, full of the spirit of the Lord in every part.

precepts.text: Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant, but he knoweth not that the dead are there, and that her guests are in the depths of hell.
precepts.point: The other side of the promise is that an unjust balance shortens your days. One day somebody realizes you have been robbing them, and men kill over a dollar. The Lord wrote that from the beginning.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Stolen waters are sweet, and bread eaten in secret is pleasant.” You feel good when you make that extra money from tilting the scale, when you are stealing. It tastes sweet.

“But he knoweth not that the dead are there; and that her guests are in the depths of hell.” What he does not know is where it leads: death and condemnation. The one who eats the stolen bread is sitting among the dead.

So do not be a thief. Deal righteously; deal according to the law, statutes and commandments. The divers weights of Deuteronomy 25 are stolen waters, and the days they seem to add are really shortened, just as the law warned: the just weight is “that thy days may be lengthened in the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.”

And pride keeps a man from hearing it: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Once people have a little money in their pocket, they feel grown and will not seek counsel, and when everything falls apart, then they want counsel. The scriptures say blessed is he that readeth; if we apply what we read, we will be all right.

70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

points: Reprove not a scorner, lest he hate thee. The scorner does not want to hear how the Bible has the solutions to fix his life; he wants to hear that he can keep living in debauchery. That is a destroyed mind.

Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee. That is every brother and sister in here: we all got rebuked at one time or another, and we said, I want to learn more, because I know that is the word of God.
